details:
To the VRC Development and Operations Team:

The “new arm movement feature” that was just implemented recently has the wheel click assigned to it, which means I can no longer intuitively rotate and adjust objects I’ve grabbed with the mouse. Whether by separating these functions, making them toggleable in settings, or introducing a toggle key—I’d really like to continue using the original functionality if possible.

I apologize for speaking from my own perspective, but I log into VRC in desktop mode and use a QV pen to leave notes, draw pictures, and so on. Since I need to hold the pen in my hand and adjust the tip’s orientation, I often used the wheel click to rotate it.

With the addition of this new feature, I now feel that little joys—like adjusting the orientation or playing around with items—have been significantly lost…

It feels as though, in exchange for being able to move my arm “unrestrictedly,” my hand has been severed at the wrist.

P.S.

For 1,000 yen on Booth, I could have added equivalent functionality at my own discretion and toggled it via the menu. Even though it’s free, the trade-off for this “compatible” feature is a loss of (my) comfort, so it ultimately feels like a downgrade.

I hate to sound repetitive, but the joy of moving my arm doesn’t balance out the comfort I’ve lost in so many areas. If they’re going to make rotation happen with keys, shouldn’t they also include a feature to faintly display the item’s coordinate system? It’s so incredibly hard to tell where things are that I used to do it intuitively with the mouse wheel.

Sorry for relying on a translation app ＆if I posted this in the wrong place

From a user in Jp
title: Drawbacks of Implementing a New Feature That Allows Arm Movement
